evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Iran weighs allowing Europe to clear mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
evidence.snippet: Iran is considering allowing European nations to remove mines from the Strait of Hormuz, a concession that could be part of a deal to normalise shipping in the waterway and ease peace talks with the United States. Iran has repeatedly stated in public that it will not allow foreign countries to participate in demining efforts at the critical oil and liquefied natural gas transportation hub. However, in private meetings in recent weeks, Tehran has softened its stance, according to diplomats familiar with the situation who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive matters. The Iranian foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Morgan Stanley: Fed Reaction Function Comes Under Scrutiny

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Morgan Stanley: Fed Reaction Function Comes Under Scrutiny
evidence.snippet: Last week showed that central bank decisions and market reactions do not always move together. The Fed, Bank of England and Bank of Japan all left policy unchanged, but the Fed produced the strongest response. Three dissents in favour of a hike showed how close the Committee may be to tightening, while markets had priced around a one-third chance of a move. The press conference triggered the bigger reaction, with short-term yields falling and longer-dated Treasuries selling off. Breakevens widened, the dollar weakened and risk assets came under pressure as investors reassessed how the new Chair intends to return inflation to target. Although subsequent core PCE data confirmed that inflation is softening, markets remain uncertain about the Fed’s reaction function and have not fully accepted that further hikes are off the table.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: JPMorgan: Japan and the US Coordinate to Resist Yen Weakness

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: JPMorgan: Japan and the US Coordinate to Resist Yen Weakness
evidence.snippet: Japan’s Ministry of Finance appears to have conducted yen-buying intervention on both July 30 and 31, with total intervention this year likely already well above the ¥15 trillion used in 2024. The Financial Times also reported coordinated US intervention for the first time since June 1998, suggesting cooperation between US and Japanese authorities to prevent further yen depreciation is stronger than previously expected. The reported US action appears to have involved buying yen against the euro rather than the dollar, indicating support for Japan’s intervention rather than an attempt to weaken the dollar more broadly. Japanese authorities clearly view USD/JPY above 160 as excessive and are unwilling to tolerate it. Seeking US support may also reflect limits on further unilateral intervention and Japan’s inability to accelerate BoJ rate hikes solely to stop yen weakness.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Bank of America: Warsh Was Dovish, but September Hike Risk Remains

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Bank of America: Warsh Was Dovish, but September Hike Risk Remains
evidence.snippet: Warsh’s July press conference struck a dovish tone and offered little clarity, prompting a rise in long-end yields led by breakevens and renewed questions over Fed credibility. The need to restore that credibility could increase the likelihood of a September hike, supporting the forecast for 25bp hikes at each of the remaining three meetings this year. The July jobs and CPI reports will be crucial. Soft data would validate Warsh’s stance, while firm data would put the focus on the yield curve: flattening would suggest confidence that the Fed will act, while steepening would signal that policy is falling behind the curve. July payrolls are expected to rise by 80,000, with private payrolls up 95,000, while unemployment is forecast to edge up to 4.3% as participation rebounds. A result in line with these forecasts would support the view that labour-market downside risks have faded and reinforce the case for three further hikes.

evidence.snippet: 정부가 2026년 세제개편안에서 가상자산 과세를 다시 미루지 않았습니다. 현행법대로라면 코인 과세는 2027년 1월 1일부터 시작됩니다. 하지만 국세청 통합분석시스템은 아직 구축 중이고, 스테이킹·에어드랍 같은 세부 기준도 남아 있습니다. 그럼에도 정부가 일정을 유지하는 이유는 무엇일까요. 이번 영상에서는 세 차례 유예의 이유와 현재 준비 상태를 비교해 봅니다. 결론은 준비 완료보다 ‘선시행 후 보완’에 가깝습니다. #비트코인 #가상자산과세 #코인세금 #세제개편안 #코인과세 🔔 구독과 좋아요는 영상 제작에 큰 힘이 됩니다. ⚠️ [면책 조항 / Disclaimer] 본 채널의 모든 콘텐츠는 정보 제공 및 교육을 목적으로 제작되었으며, 투자를 유도하거나 특정 자산의 매수/매도를 권유하지 않습니다. 모든 투자의 판단과 책임은 투자자 본인에게 있음을 명시합니다.
